content:
Now in docgen, there is a known problem that it cannot print the scoped notations.

#general > docgen scoped notations @ 💬

The main problem was that once the source is compiled, the scope information of the definition are lost, so there is no way to know what scopes to open when printing. This is fine for globally defined notations but it cannot reflect the local notations.

Currently there is a RFC lean4#6050 about this, but there is no progress as long as I know.

motivated by this post, I made a different approach to successfully print the scoped notations.

For example, 

inductive testNotations :Type
| test : testNotations

namespace ScopedNotation

scoped notation "^_^" => testNotations.test
scoped notation "°Д°;" => testNotations

end ScopedNotation

def unscopedDef : testNotations := testNotations.test

section

open scoped ScopedNotation

def scopedDef : °Д°; := ^_^

end

The algorithm works like this:
It finds the source file and do the elaboration which are related to the scope operations (open, namespace...). And if something is defined then it captures the scope and use it when pretty printing.

By this way I could print the notations in mathlib which are bind to some scopes.

Note that this is just an estimation, so there may be a possibility to reflect the scope not correctly. To know the exact scope, we should do every elaboration one by one, and that is exactly same as compiling the source again. I think that would take lot of resources.

However, this heuristic works enough for the most of the existing mathlib files and I thought this way is better than just waiting the RFC to be solved. (And Maybe it is better way than RFC since there are no needs except for the documents to include redundant scope data in the olean file.)

Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.Notation

Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Limits.Shapes.Diagonal
